We need solve this SWE-bench task. Modify the repository to fix the issue, then leave the working tree with the patch applied.

Set disabled prop on ReadOnlyPasswordHashField
Description

Currently the django.contrib.auth.forms.UserChangeForm defines a clean_password method that returns the initial password value to prevent (accidental) changes to the password value. It is also documented that custom forms for the User model need to define this method: ​https://docs.djangoproject.com/en/3.1/topics/auth/customizing/#a-full-example
A while ago the forms.Field base class gained the ​disabled argument to:
[disable] a form field using the disabled HTML attribute so that it won’t be editable by users. Even if a user tampers with the field’s value submitted to the server, it will be ignored in favor of the value from the form’s initial data.
It seems to me that this property could be set to True be default on the ReadOnlyPasswordHashField used to display the password hash. This way the clean_password is no longer necessary and the potential pitfall when using the ReadOnlyPasswordHashField without implementing clean_password is removed.

content.text: I’ll inspect the auth form field and its tests first, then make the smallest code and test changes that capture the disabled-field behavior.

The repository is clean except for an untracked `.codex` entry, which I’ll leave alone. I found the password hash field and the existing auth form tests, so I’m reading those sections now to line up the fix with Django’s current patterns.

The disabled machinery already exists in `forms.Field`: a disabled field cleans from initial data and ignores submitted values. The auth field currently duplicates part of that with `bound_data()` and `has_changed()`, while `UserChangeForm.clean_password()` handles cleaning, so I’m going to move that responsibility onto `ReadOnlyPasswordHashField` and update the docs example accordingly.

I’m applying a focused patch now: default the auth password hash field to `disabled=True`, drop the redundant `UserChangeForm.clean_password()`, and add a regression test showing a standalone custom `ModelForm` is protected without defining `clean_password()`.
The code and docs patches are in place. I’m running the targeted auth form tests now, since they exercise both the built-in `UserChangeForm` and the custom-form regression path.
The first test command failed because `django` wasn’t on `PYTHONPATH` in this checkout. I’m rerunning the same targeted tests with `PYTHONPATH=.` so the local package is imported.

That rerun gets further but the environment’s default Python is missing `distutils`, which this Django branch imports. I’m checking whether another Python executable with `distutils` is available before treating that as a hard test-environment blocker.

There isn’t a usable `setuptools._distutils` fallback either. I’m checking for installed `packaging` so I can run the targeted tests with a temporary `distutils.version.LooseVersion` shim outside the repository, without adding anything to the patch.

To verify despite the missing stdlib module, I’m invoking the test runner through a short in-memory shim that supplies only the `LooseVersion.version` behavior this branch uses. This keeps the repository patch limited to the actual fix.

The shim cleared `distutils`, but the environment also lacks Django’s runtime dependency `asgiref`. I’m looking for any existing local environment or installed package path before I stop trying full test execution.
